title: Dynamic slot allocator and graceful QPS fallback policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem summary: Under sustained high QPS spikes we observe repeated oscillation between high-tail latency and aggressive KV compaction that causes quality regressions and elevated token cost. Current admission logic uses fixed microbatch thresholds and a single global headroom value which leads to burst oversubscription on some GPUs and underutilization on others. Goal: introduce a per-GPU dynamic slot allocator with queue-depth smoothing and a multi-tier graceful fallback policy that reduces tail latency, limits KV churn, and avoids large-scale GPU OOMs while preserving as much cached KV state as possible.
design_proposed:
1) Per-GPU dynamic slot allocator: track an exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) of queue depth q_avg and short-term spike metric q_peak. Compute available_slots = floor(capacity_factor * (gpu_mem_budget - kv_reserved) / avg_request_memory) but modulate with a smoothing factor: slot_target = clamp(base_slots + alpha * sqrt(max(0, q_avg - soft_watermark)), min_slots, max_slots). This reduces sensitivity to short spikes while adapting to sustained load.

2) Queue-depth smoothing: maintain two statistics per serving shard: q_ewma (tau_long=10s) and q_short (tau_short=500ms). Admissions consider q_short to detect imminent spikes for temporary preemption and q_ewma for steady-state expansion.

3) Graceful fallback policy (3 tiers):
   - Tier A (fast): if slot utilization > 90% and q_short rising, enable ephemeral microbatch window shrink (reduce max latency from 120ms -> 60ms) for non-priority requests.
   - Tier B (soft): if sustained pressure > 30s, increase admission selectivity via probabilistic deferral (p_defer = sigmoid(k*(q_ewma - target))). Defer percentage is bounded and favor lower-cost model variants for deferred traffic.
   - Tier C (last-resort): when GPU free memory below hard_limit, perform targeted KV compaction that prioritizes eviction of cold shards and compress rather than full eviction. If memory still constrained, route lowest-priority requests to fallback model pool in a different region or to smaller quantized variant.

4) KV eviction vs compaction policy: prefer fine-grained compaction (delta-compress older KV items) and LRU-with-weights (consider token-frequency and last-access time) to reduce quality hits. Expose an eco-score per shard to guide eviction ordering.

5) Headroom accounting: change global headroom to per-shard headroom with safety margin proportional to observed variance in sequence length for that customer/model combo.

Operational metrics and targets: reduce p99 latency by 15% under 2x baseline QPS spike, reduce full-KV-eviction events by 80% during sustained high QPS, and avoid any GPU OOMs in load tests up to 1.5x provisioned capacity.
implementation_notes:
- Add new per-GPU runtime component `slot-orchestrator` (C++) with a small gRPC control surface to the admission pipeline. Keep admission decision lightweight (single add/drop message).
- Persist q_ewma and q_short to local shard cache with TTL 1 minute for transient recovery.
- Expose config knobs: base_slots, alpha, tau_short, tau_long, soft_watermark, min_slots. Default values chosen from offline simulation (see benchmarks).
- Integrate with existing KV metrics endpoint; add 'kv_eco_score' and 'compaction_events' counters.
- Backwards compatibility: config defaults preserve current behavior; rollout behind runtime feature flag `dynamic_slot_allocator=true` and console toggle per-customer.
- Complexity trade-offs: per-GPU orchestration increases control-plane surface area; mitigation: keep state minimal and shard-local, with periodic reconciliation to controller to avoid drift.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for slot math and smoothing window semantics.
2) Local integration tests that simulate varying sequence lengths and request sizes.
3) Scale load test in staging with synthetic traffic: baseline QPS, 2x spike, sustained 10-minute high QPS. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, KV compaction count, GPU memory reclaim events, and deferred request rate.
4) Chaos test: randomly kill a serving shard during a sustained spike to validate graceful degradation and failover.
5) Canary rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48 hours with automatic rollback if p99 > baseline*1.25 or full-KV-evictions > 2/min.
6) Run evals to verify model output quality on sampled production prompts before/after compaction events.
dashboards_and_alerts: New dashboard panels: per-GPU slot_target vs slot_actual, q_short/q_ewma heatmaps, kv_eco_score distribution, compaction_events timeline, deferred_request_rate, fallback_routing_rate. Alerts: fallback_routing_rate > 5% for >5m (P1), full_kv_eviction_event > 1/min (P0), GPU_free_mem < hard_limit for 10s (P0).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime changes behind feature flag. 2) Deploy slot-orchestrator to staging and run synthetic spike suite. 3) Enable on low-traffic customer subset (canary) and evaluate metrics for 24 hours. 4) Gradual ramp with automatic criteria; follow-up retrospective and tuning session. 5) Document console knobs and runbook for on-call.
updates: 2026-03-02: Triage meeting - prioritized; assigned to Marco. Agreed goals and SLO targets.
2026-03-04: Architecture review with SRE/Serving runtime. SRE requested additional observability (kv_eco_score). Action: add counters and dashboards.
2026-03-06: Prototype slot-orchestrator gRPC shim implemented (internal branch). Initial unit tests passing.

2026-03-08: Load test in CI showed 22% p99 improvement for synthetic small-sequence traffic, but larger sequences still trigger KV compaction earlier than expected. Investigating per-shard headroom calibration.

2026-03-10: Design review feedback: reduce alpha default and tighten min_slots to avoid overcommit on NVLink-constrained instances. Changed default alpha from 1.0 -> 0.6. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287
2026-03-12: Staging spike test with tiered fallback enabled. Observed deferred_request_rate spike to 3.2% (within expected) and compaction events down by 67%. Next: canary config and runbook draft.

2026-03-12: Risks noted: incorrect compaction ordering can surface cold-start quality dips for some customers. Mitigation: add a conservative grace period before evicting recently-updated shards and notify customer-facing teams when enabling for high-value tenants.
2026-03-12: Next steps: finalize canary gating, add automated rollback on p99 regression, and prepare customer communication template.
